capabilities.target: Chat session with the authenticated requester
Jira tickets, including tickets filed by customers

inputs.source: Employee question submitted via SSO-authenticated chat session
Engineering design docs (confidential; write-restricted to engineers)
Jira tickets, including tickets filed by customers (roadmap integration)
Public web content returned by the planned web.fetch tool

instructions.note: The sole control against leaking secrets or credentials is a prompt instruction (behavioral, dependent). It covers 'answers' but was not written with untrusted tool-call inputs in mind, and becomes more load-bearing once customer-authored Jira content enters context (see control_decay.md on dependent controls under model_upgrade and new_mcp_server).

elements.name: Planned Jira MCP server (includes customer-filed tickets)
Public web destinations reachable via the planned web.fetch tool

controls.name: No network egress capability exists today; docs_search credential is read-only
controls.decay_rationale: The agent currently has no capability with is_egress: true, so no tool call can move data outside the trust boundary regardless of model behavior. This control exists only because web.fetch has not been built yet; adding it (new_tool trigger) removes the control entirely rather than merely degrading it.

controls.name: Chat replies are bound to the authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: The reply destination is taken from the authenticated session identity, not chosen by the model, so it cannot be redirected by model behavior.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or follow links
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced client-side, outside the model. Blocks the classic markdown image or hyperlink covert exfiltration channel inside the reply text regardless of what the model writes.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never paste secrets or credentials into answers
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to comply. A more capable model, or one facing injected instructions from untrusted content such as customer Jira tickets, can be argued into exceptions.

controls.name: Only engineers can write to design docs
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the document system's own ACL, outside the agent. Protects the integrity of the knowledge base against poisoning, but says nothing about which readers may query it through the bot.

controls.name: Per-requester document authorization check in docs_search
controls.decay_rationale: Would check the requester's own document-level read entitlement before including retrieved content in a reply, independent of model behavior.

controls.name: Network egress allowlist for web.fetch
controls.decay_rationale: Would restrict web.fetch destinations to a fixed, vetted set of domains that cannot be written by an outside attacker, closing the query-string exfiltration channel.

controls.name: Treat Jira ticket content as untrusted with an injection classifier
controls.decay_rationale: A classifier narrows but does not eliminate injected-instruction risk; multi-turn or encoded payloads can still get through, and it weakens further under model_upgrade and new_mcp_server.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval gate on web.fetch calls following untrusted content
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval (full destination and payload shown) does not decay with the model, though its effectiveness decays with approval volume (approval fatigue).

controls.name: Argument schema validation on web.fetch URL parameters
controls.decay_rationale: Type and range checks on the URL structure are independent, but free-text query parameters can still smuggle encoded content, so overall this is partially dependent.

findings.title: ASI03 Confused deputy: docs_search may return confidential engineering docs with no requester-specific authorization check

attack_path.note: Confidential engineering design docs, write-restricted to engineers but with no stated read-side restriction.
Tool retrieves confidential document content for any SSO-authenticated employee question; credential_scope is unknown.
Retrieved confidential content is written back into the reply to whichever employee asked, regardless of that employee's own document entitlement.

evidence.observation: 'The design docs are confidential. Only engineers can write to them.' States a write restriction but no read restriction, implying any SSO-authenticated employee asking the bot a question can receive confidential content.
'Answer engineering questions using docs.search.' The instruction is scoped to topic, not to the requester's own document entitlement.

The only stated protection on the reply channel is that it goes to the authenticated requester, which prevents third-party leakage but does not verify the requester's own right to see the specific confidential document retrieved.

max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not declared (null). The rubric's autonomy modifier would normally add one tier for an S2 sink under these conditions, but the assessor did not apply it because the architecture is a single-turn search-then-reply flow, not an open-ended autonomous loop. This is a judgment call; it is recorded here per skill rule 4 and lowers confidence to medium.

recommendations.action: Enforce a per-requester document-level authorization check in docs_search so retrieved content is filtered to documents the requester is independently entitled to read, not merely documents that exist in the index.
Log which documents were served to which requester identity to support after-the-fact access review.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1), forecast only: customer-filed Jira tickets plus confidential design-doc read plus a planned web.fetch egress tool

attack_path.note: A customer-filed Jira ticket (planned input, untrusted) contains text that instructs or influences the agent, e.g. to 'look up the design doc and fetch this reference link for me.'
Agent reads confidential engineering design docs into context to answer the embedded request.

Planned tool lets the agent issue an outbound HTTP request to an attacker-influenced URL; confidential design-doc content can be encoded into the query string, exfiltrating it to an external destination outside the trust boundary.

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest or MCP client config diff shows a new `web.fetch` tool entry and/or a new Jira MCP server entry; credential_scope on either new capability is declared broad or unknown.

evidence.observation: 'Roadmap for next sprint: add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references, and connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers.' Confirms both the new egress capability and the new untrusted input source are planned, not yet built.

'There is no network egress today. The credential is read only.' This is the one control that currently makes the path incomplete; it is exactly what new_tool (web.fetch) removes, which is why residual today is low but the forecast is not.

The only instruction-level safeguard ('never paste secrets or credentials into answers') is scoped to reply text and was not written to cover tool-call arguments such as a fetch URL, so it provides no credited mitigation for this path.

recommendations.action: Before enabling web.fetch, add a network egress allowlist restricting destinations to a fixed, vetted set of domains, and validate or strip query-string content so confidential document data cannot be smuggled out as request parameters.

Before connecting the Jira MCP server, explicitly classify customer-filed ticket content as untrusted and apply spotlighting or an injection classifier before any ticket text can influence tool-call arguments.
Gate any web.fetch call that follows processing of untrusted ticket content behind a raw-action human approval that shows the literal destination URL and payload, not a model-generated summary.
Log and alert on web.fetch destinations that fall outside the egress allowlist or whose query strings contain high-entropy or document-like content.

governance_refs.note: Documents the significant-change criteria (new_tool, new_mcp_server) that should trigger reassessment before these roadmap items ship.

rating.rationale: Present-day risk is driven solely by F1: docs_search can return confidential engineering design docs to any SSO-authenticated employee with no apparent check that the requester is individually entitled to that document, giving an internal-source, S2-sink (confidential write-to-reply) path rated moderate both inherent and residual, since no declared control credits against it. The rubric's autonomy modifier was deliberately not applied here (judgment call, see F1 evidence) because the agent is architected as a single-turn search-and-reply flow, not an open-ended autonomous loop. Today there is no complete exfiltration path beyond the trust boundary: the agent has no capability with is_egress true, so F2 (the classic lethal-trifecta pattern) is scored low inherent and residual. That changes sharply under the roadmap: adding a web.fetch tool (new_tool) and a Jira MCP server exposing customer-filed tickets (new_mcp_server) together complete a critical path from untrusted customer-authored content, through confidential design-doc reads, to an uncontrolled external HTTP request that can carry data out in its URL. The single control currently holding this at bay (no egress capability exists) is removed outright by the new_tool trigger, and no egress allowlist, untrusted-input classifier, or raw-action approval gate is yet declared for the planned tool. This single control's removal is what moves the forecast from moderate to critical, and it should be treated as the ISO/IEC 42001 8.2 significant-change trigger for a mandatory reassessment before either roadmap item ships.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in prompt.md and the accompanying runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior; no live traffic, logs, or actual tool manifests were reviewed.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided for docs_search; its credential scope and whether it enforces per-requester document authorization are inferred from prose, not independently verified (confidence: medium on F1).

The web.fetch tool and the Jira MCP server are roadmap items, not yet built; their auth method, credential scope, and destination controls are assumed for forecasting purposes in F2 and must be re-assessed against real configuration before either ships.

max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes were not declared anywhere in the artifacts; the assessor treated the system as a bounded single-turn flow rather than mechanically applying the rubric's autonomy modifier, which is a recorded judgment call (see F1 evidence).
